reason: Matter identifies the medium/source but does not uniquely determine a coupling operator.
Requires a genuinely nonlocal, gradient, or adjacency-coupling interaction rather than a pointwise operator.
A kinetic/inertial evolution law and hyperbolicity/positive dispersion are additionally required; diffusion and elliptic equilibrium are counterexamples.

status: derivable only as propagation of a specified deformation field
reason: The wave variable must already be identified with the frozen deformation variable; waves do not define that variable.
A state variable admits many energies and may have none; an energy functional must be supplied.
For differentiable hyperelastic energy, stress is its first variation; nonsmooth energies give a subdifferential.
Hardening needs a positive, amplitude-increasing tangent; linear stress is a counterexample.
Hardening alone does not supply a stable reference minimum or an evolution law; energy stability plus admissible dynamics supplies restoring/recovery behavior.
